text:
sre-bot: ALERT: gpu-pool-4 (eu-central-1) degraded -> 40% healthy. 2x p4d hosts reporting NIC flaps, packet loss spike. Auto-evac attempted but some shards still draining.
Maya Chen: seeing the alert — any planned maintenance?
Priya Singh: not on our calendar. I’m checking power/grid alerts.
Jorge Alvarez: infra-monitor shows upstream ISP B peering flaps at 14:12 UTC, link flaps correlate with host errors. graph: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/xyz/eu-pool?orgId=1
Maya Chen: ok can we start a soft traffic shift before more requests queue? latency already creeping for eu clients.
Liam O'Connor: I can apply a weighted steer via global router. prefer soft drain to avoid error spikes.
Anika Patel: flag cost implications — shifting a large portion of EU -> NA will spike cross-region egress and instance CPU on NA. watch billing alerts.
sre-bot: runbook step recommended: "soft-evac via gslb override" -> set eu weight to 0.2 then ramp.
Priya Singh: also consider local fallback to smaller quantized models in eu to keep more traffic local. cheaper than full cross-region egress for small workloads.
Maya Chen: agreed. plan: 1) apply soft evacs (eu 0.2) 2) enable eu fallback model where possible 3) monitor latency & error rates, iterate.
Liam O'Connor: running command now:
```
# opsctl gslb override set --region eu-central-1 --weight 0.2 --reason "NIC-flap-soft-evac"
# opsctl gslb override adjust --region na-west-1 --weight +0.5 --region apac-south-1 --weight +0.3
```
Liam O'Connor: pushed override at 14:22 UTC. preview: eu=0.18 na=0.62 apac=0.20 (soft ramp)
deploy-bot: Canary traffic check: 200 requests proxied through new weights -> 0 errors, p50=78ms, p95=210ms (within SLO for canary).
Maya Chen: good. Priya, can you toggle model fallback for the top 3 EU routes?
Priya Singh: doing it for: chat-gen, embed, rerank. command:
```
servicectl set-model --service chat-gen --region eu-central-1 --model redwood-base-quant --min-instances 2
servicectl set-model --service embed --region eu-central-1 --model tiny-embed-quant --min-instances 1
servicectl set-model --service rerank --region eu-central-1 --model rerank-light --min-instances 1
```
Priya Singh: changes applied at 14:29 UTC. scaling policies left aggressive to allow local handling.
Jorge Alvarez: network team says ISPs report a partial backbone outage affecting eu-central backbone X. ETA unclear.
Anika Patel: opened billing watch with finance — set temporary threshold + alert. Also raising a note: customers on reserved workloads might be impacted; we should exempt them from aggressive steering if they have isolation requirements.
Maya Chen: acknowledged. I’ll pin list of reserved-customer routes and exempt them from weight adjustments.
Liam O'Connor: metrics after 10m: EU error rate down 70%, queue length decreasing, cross-region egress up ~28% — within predicted range.
sre-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-345 (eu-central network flap). Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-345
Maya Chen: set oncall->pager for network lead, requesting immediate peering reroute with ISP B.
Jorge Alvarez: adding note — KV cache miss rate increased slightly due to traffic mixing; recommend short-lived cache warming and allow 5m for steady state.
Priya Singh: also toggled prefix caching TTL from 300 -> 120 for EU fallbacks to reduce stale responses.
Anika Patel: cost check: if we keep current weights > 30% cross-region for >2 hours, projected overage ~ $9k. Approve continued steering?
Maya Chen: keep steering for now but reduce NA increment if egress costs spike. We’ll auto-roll back to per-customer defaults at 18:00 UTC if no fix.
Liam O'Connor: noted. I’ll create a scheduled job to revert overrides at 18:00 unless manually extended:
```
opsctl gslb override schedule-cancel --id 1921509876 --at 18:00UTC
```
Maya Chen: thanks. action items: 1) network team escalate with ISP B (Jorge) 2) oncall monitoring + alerts (Liam) 3) finance watch (Anika) 4) keep soft-evac in place, continue model fallbacks (Priya).
Liam O'Connor: will monitor for error spikes and roll to full evac (eu=0.0) if host failures exceed threshold.
sre-bot: update: host replacement kicked for 2 affected p4d nodes, ETA 45m.
Maya Chen: good to hear. we’ll keep channel open. add any client-impact notes to the incident page. :white_check_mark:
Priya Singh: adding remediation steps and model fallback rationale to INC-2026-345.
Jorge Alvarez: ISP B confirms BGP reroute request accepted, propagation expected within 20-40m.
Anika Patel: logging cost delta in incident to billback later.
Maya Chen: thanks all — close this thread once we confirm stable metrics and incident updated.
Liam O'Connor: updating last metrics at 14:58 UTC: eu error rate ~2% (back to baseline 0.8% after replacements), queue near-normal. scheduling rollback window 18:00 still in place.
sre-bot: RESOLVED (monitoring): gpu-pool-4 restored to 92% healthy after host replacements and ISP reroute.
Maya Chen: moving to post-incident review tomorrow 09:30 UTC. invite list: Maya, Liam, Priya, Jorge, Anika, network lead.
Maya Chen: thread closed for operational actions; keep incident page open for docs."
